cover.headline: Five questions every club answers all week long.

inner.headline: What time does the grill close tonight?
inner.body: Asked from the course, the pool deck and the parking lot.

inner.headline: Is the pool open Monday?
inner.body: Especially the Monday after a holiday weekend.

inner.headline: What is the guest policy this weekend?
What do I wear to Friday dinner?
inner.body: The answer is published. The question still comes.

close.headline: None of these are hard. That is the point.
close.body: Each one is small, and each one interrupts someone on the team.
close.tryBody: Count the routine questions your team answers on one Saturday.

caption:
Five small questions, asked all week, from everywhere.

They arrive by phone, by text, at the pro shop counter and in the hallway, and each one lands on someone in the middle of something else. A dining manager setting up for service. A pro between lessons. A membership director on a call.

Every answer is on file somewhere. What costs the club is the interruption, repeated all week.
firstComment: Which question would top the list at your club?

earnsItsPlace: Names the routine questions Club Pilot answers so staff are not interrupted, from the operator's side of the counter; a vendor that only sends announcements has nothing to say about the questions that come back.
